prompt: Compute the surface area of a rectangular prism with side lengths $2$, $3$, $4$.

solutions.title: Telescoping product
solutions.body:
$S_k=\frac{k(k+1)}2$ and $S_k-1=\frac{k^2+k-2}{2}=\frac{(k-1)(k+2)}2$, so $\frac{S_k}{S_k-1}=\frac{k}{k-1}\cdot\frac{k+1}{k+2}$.

Then $\prod_{k=2}^n\frac k{k-1}=n$ and $\prod_{k=2}^n\frac{k+1}{k+2}=\frac{3}{n+2}$, so $T_n=\frac{3n}{n+2}$ and $T_{2015}=\frac{6045}{2017}$.

**Answer: $\frac{6045}{2017}$**

prompt: A bag contains $12$ marbles: $3$ red, $4$ green, and $5$ blue. Repeatedly draw marbles with replacement until you draw two marbles of the same color in a row. What is the expected number of times that you will draw a marble?

solutions.title: Condition on the last color
solutions.body:
Colour probabilities: $p_R=\frac14$, $p_G=\frac13$, $p_B=\frac5{12}$. Let $E_c$ be the expected number of further draws given the last draw had colour $c$. Then $E_c=1+\sum_{d\ne c}p_dE_d$ (the next draw is made; the process continues only if the colour changes). Writing $S=p_RE_R+p_GE_G+p_BE_B$, we have $E_c=1+S-p_cE_c$, so $E_c=\frac{1+S}{1+p_c}$.

Then $S=\sum_cp_c\frac{1+S}{1+p_c}=(1+S)\sum_c\frac{p_c}{1+p_c}$. Here $\sum\frac{p_c}{1+p_c}=\frac{1/4}{5/4}+\frac{1/3}{4/3}+\frac{5/12}{17/12}=\frac15+\frac14+\frac5{17}=\frac{68+85+100}{340}=\frac{253}{340}$. So $S=\frac{253/340}{87/340}=\frac{253}{87}$.

The total expected number of draws is $1+S=\frac{340}{87}$.

**Answer: $\frac{340}{87}$**
